notes:
POC focused on infra guarantees. Key friction: Veridian runs live product recommendations with millisecond sensitivity during flash sales. They want hard guarantees (min tokens/sec) rather than best-effort.
- Quote from CTO: "If the engine stalls during a promo we lose millions in GMV — need hard floor."
- They measured 220ms p99 at 6 GPUs in our hosted demo but saw 350ms spikes during cold restart.
- Ask: explicit concurrency caps with clear behavior when exceeded (queue vs reject), and a burst policy that favors short lived bursts without penalizing committed throughput.
- They prefer H100-class hardware; willing to sign 12–24mo commit if SLA covers min throughput and crediting.
- Risk: they are cost-sensitive around overage; insist on predictable cost model for burst consumption.
- SE notes: recommend reserved pool + autoscale buffer (burst tokens bucket) + explicit SLO credit formula: credit = max(0, (min_tokens/sec - observed_tokens/sec)/min_tokens/sec) * committed_monthly_fee (subject to cap).
- Security: need KMS integration and SOC2 audit report; Veridian will run internal security questionnaire week of 2026-03-15.
- Next: finalize hardware/price appendix and SLA section on min_tokens/sec by 2026-03-22.
